overview.text: The Inland Taipan has the most toxic venom of any land snake in laboratory tests on mice. Yet it is far from the most dangerous snake to people: it is shy, prefers to escape, and lives in remote, dry inland Australia, so bites are very rare.

identification.text: A medium-large elapid whose colour changes with the seasons: darker in winter and paler in summer. The darker winter colour probably helps it soak up more of the sun's heat when it is cold.

size.label: Adults
size.text: Sources give lengths of around 1.8 to 2.5 m, with about 2 m typical.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: Found only in Australia: south-western Queensland and north-eastern and central South Australia.

habitat.text: Remote semi-arid country in the interior of Australia.

behaviour.text: Very shy: it nearly always tries to flee rather than defend itself.

diet.text: Mostly small mammals. Its favourite prey is the Long-haired Rat; it also eats house mice and small marsupials called dasyurids.

reproduction.text: Lays eggs; one source reports clutches of 12 to 20 eggs that hatch after about 66 days.

funfacts.text: In tests on mice, the venom from one bite would be enough to kill around 250,000 mice.
It turns darker in winter, like putting on a heat-absorbing coat.
